# Assessment definitions and compiler boundary

These are synthetic definitions for Codex 0.149.1 and Devin 3000.10.21. They are
not production Profile fields or an extension installer. Nothing executes them.
The JSON, TOML and Markdown are vendor-facing representations; the Go test does
not implement or claim to replace either vendor's parser.

`definition_prototypes_test.go` selects each complete plugin directory, role,
hook definition and input as read-only data through the real common capability
codecs and each target's registry. It resolves the actual executable grant for
the hook witness, calls `Plan`, and calls `Materialize`. Removing either the
selected role or executable makes the corresponding real grant resolution fail.
The read-only workspace already permits reading these files; these selections
do not claim additional effective authority or isolation inside that workspace.

For the plugin's one Skill, the assessment explicitly stages the selected bundle
in the existing `shared-agents` source. This is component extraction, **not plugin
discovery or installation**. Production materialization is checked byte-for-byte:

| Output | Codex | Devin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common component | `.acs/common/v1/skills/shared-agents/reviewer/SKILL.md` | same |
| Target component | `.codex/skills/shared-agents/reviewer/SKILL.md` | `.agents/skills/reviewer/SKILL.md` |

The entire generated file inventory must equal those two files. Thus a selected
role file or hook JSON is not mistaken for an activated extension. The Codex
plan's registered `codex.plugins=disabled` decision is also asserted.

## Concrete fields outside the current compiler

| Definition | Representable selected requirements | Unrepresented target semantics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex `plugin/plugin.json` plus conventional `skills/` | Read-only package and explicit Skill component | Plugin name/install identity, marketplace enablement and trust, persistent `PLUGIN_DATA`, dependencies/update/removal. Codex plugin activation is explicitly disabled by the current production plan. |
| Devin `plugin/.devin-plugin/plugin.json`, `skills:["./skills/reviewer"]` | Same selected package and component | Local installation/enablement and authentication, manifest precedence, plugin namespacing, governance, dependencies and persistent data. No linked installation is performed. |
| Codex `agents/reviewer.toml` | Read-only selected definition and input | Discovery under `$CODEX_HOME/agents`, role selection/spawn, `developer_instructions`, and `features.shell_tool=false`. The pinned role allowlist does **not** confer a new OS sandbox, network or environment grant; these must not be invented as arbitrary role overrides. |
| Devin `agents/reviewer.md` | Read-only selected definition and input | Discovery under `.devin/agents` or user agent sources, frontmatter `allowed-tools`, prompt injection and orchestration. `allowed-tools: [read]` is a target tool restriction, not an ACS per-agent filesystem sandbox. |
| Codex `hooks.json` with outer `hooks` | Read-only definition/input and selected executable | `SessionStart` event binding, command shell/stdin/stdout ABI, timeout, trust and child settlement. No hook file is generated by production materialization. |
| Devin standalone `hooks.v1.json` without outer `hooks` | Same selected resources | Project `.devin/hooks.v1.json` discovery, event/matcher and command ABI, timeout and lifecycle semantics. The separate native assessment, not this test, is responsible for execution evidence. |

These differences require target overlays or further assessment; the fixture does
not classify arbitrary extensions by name or pretend common references encode
these semantics. No assertion here establishes target parser acceptance, actual
discovery, model obedience, trust approval, descendant cleanup or native safety.
A future contained probe must deliberately place the definition at the listed
vendor discovery path and use the real selection/trust flow. Merely selecting a
read-only file is insufficient.

## Pinned primary basis

Codex source at commit
[`ff29a44391deccde0aba0f8390337d7f3c319ea4`](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/ff29a44391deccde0aba0f8390337d7f3c319ea4):

- [`core-plugins/src/agent_plugin_manifest.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ff29a44391deccde0aba0f8390337d7f3c319ea4/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/agent_plugin_manifest.rs), root schema/name and conventional `skills` (lines 64–195).
- [`core/src/config/agent_roles.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ff29a44391deccde0aba0f8390337d7f3c319ea4/codex-rs/core/src/config/agent_roles.rs), discovery and role metadata; [`core/src/agent/role.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ff29a44391deccde0aba0f8390337d7f3c319ea4/codex-rs/core/src/agent/role.rs), typed role allowlist (lines 35–125).
- [`config/src/hook_config.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ff29a44391deccde0aba0f8390337d7f3c319ea4/codex-rs/config/src/hook_config.rs), standalone outer `hooks`, command handler and timeout representation. Runtime/trust behavior is separately discussed in the assessment document.

Devin's locked Darwin arm64 archive SHA-256 is
`c0b97f8197bf3ce895ff14aa19257c511154b49a0a195bba4962acb5e475c68e`.
Its bundled `share/devin/docs/extensibility/plugins/overview.mdx` documents the
manifest and skills paths (lines 26–41, 79–101, 199–241);
`share/devin/docs/subagents.mdx` documents Markdown frontmatter, discovery and
`allowed-tools`; `share/devin/docs/extensibility/hooks/overview.mdx` and
`lifecycle-hooks.mdx` document standalone hooks and SessionStart. These are
version-attributed documentation, not independent target runtime observations.
